summary: This script populates a demo Atuin shell history database with realistic command records spanning several weeks. It reads a predefined table of commands with metadata, converts them into SQLite INSERT statements with proper timestamps and escaped values, and executes them all in a single transaction to avoid timestamp collisions.

explanations.25: This line makes the script strict: it exits immediately if any command fails (set -e), treats undefined variables as errors (set -u), and fails if any command in a pipeline fails (set -o pipefail).
explanations.30: We run a dummy Atuin search to trigger database initialization and migrations before we try writing to it; the '|| true' prevents the script from failing if the search has no results.
explanations.38: We're checking if the history table already has rows; if it does, we skip seeding because the container may have been restarted and we don't want duplicate data.
explanations.42: We capture the current Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch) so we can calculate past times relative to 'now' for each seeded command.
explanations.51: This helper function generates a random 16-byte blob, converts it to hexadecimal, and lowercases it — this creates a unique ID suitable for Atuin's schema.
explanations.64: We're using 'read -r -d \'\'\'' to read a multiline string into a variable; the '|| true' prevents failure if the string doesn't end with the delimiter.
explanations.125: We're adding a small jitter (7 nanoseconds per row) to each timestamp so commands with the same minutes_ago value don't violate the unique constraint.
explanations.126: We convert minutes and jitter into nanoseconds (the unit Atuin's schema expects): first subtract from 'now', multiply by 60 to get seconds, then by 1 billion to get nanoseconds.
explanations.137: The '#HOME' syntax removes 'HOME' from the start of the cwd string and replaces it with the actual $HOME directory path.
explanations.139: In SQL strings, single quotes need to be escaped by doubling them; this replaces each \' with \'\'\' so the SQL parser treats it as a literal quote.
explanations.141: We're generating a single INSERT statement per row; the printf formats the command, working directory, and other metadata into the SQL syntax.
explanations.145: We pipe all the accumulated SQL (wrapped in BEGIN/COMMIT for a single transaction) to sqlite3, which executes them all at once against the Atuin database.
